evidence: createApp builds TaskManagementService with InMemory*Repository instances, which is composition-root wiring and fits infrastructure
Route handlers (app.post('/projects/:projectId/tasks'), app.put('/tasks/:taskId/assignee'), and others) only extract request data and call svc methods
Validation in the task routes checks types and the enum using the domain's isTaskStatus, which is input parsing at the transport layer
The error middleware maps ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError to HTTP 400, 404 and 409, which is transport concern
toDto serializes dueDate to an ISO string for the HTTP response, which is presentation and transport formatting
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/app.ts is an HTTP adapter built on Express, and it also acts as the composition root. It wires the service to in-memory repositories, registers routes, parses request input, converts tasks to DTOs and turns domain errors into HTTP status codes. All of this is infrastructure work. It defers every business operation to TaskManagementService: createUser, createProject, addTask, listTasks, assignTask and completeTask. The inline checks in the POST and GET task routes look at the shape and type of incoming data, such as whether status is a valid enum value, whether assigneeId is a string, and whether a query value is single-valued. The enum check calls the domain's own isTaskStatus predicate rather than defining the rule itself. These checks are transport-level input guarding, not business invariants or workflow rules. No persistence logic or domain logic is implemented in the file.
